blocks.caption: The principle
blocks.title: How to read this report.
blocks.lead: This report combines two levels: your genetics — inherited and unchangeable — and your epigenetics, which can be influenced by lifestyle.

cards.title: Level 1 · Genetics
cards.text: Your genes are the blueprint of your metabolism: how you process carbohydrates, fats and proteins, how appetite and satiety work, how your body handles vitamins and salt. These predispositions do not change.
items: SNP — a well-researched variant in your DNA.
Three forms — wild type, heterozygous or homozygous; without any value judgement.
Your profile — several SNPs together produce your metabolic type and evaluations.

cards.title: Level 2 · Epigenetics
cards.text: Epigenetics does not show which genes you have, but how active they currently are. These four values can be changed — and are therefore the only ones in which the effect of an intervention can be demonstrated over time.
items: LINE-1 — global DNA regulation and stability.
Inflammation regulation — combined score from IL-6 and TNF-α.
miR-21 · miR-155 — microRNAs of metabolic activity.

blocks.scaleTitle: How do I read the scale?
blocks.scaleLead: All evaluations — genetic and epigenetic alike — use the same traffic light 1–9. Red on the left, green on the right: 1–3 red, 4–6 amber, 7–9 green. Higher is always more favourable.

scaleZones.label: 1–3 · Red
scaleZones.text: Outside the optimal range. This is where the greatest leverage lies.

scaleZones.label: 4–6 · Amber
scaleZones.text: Moderate need for support. Monitor specifically.

scaleZones.label: 7–9 · Green
scaleZones.text: In the favourable range. Maintain existing routines.

blocks.title: Important
items: This report is not a diagnosis. Interpretation takes place in consultation with qualified professionals and always in the individual context.
Information and written consent are required before a genetic analysis (German Genetic Diagnostics Act, GenDG).
The genetic values never change. Only the four epigenetic values are suitable for monitoring progress.

blocks.lead: These four markers change through diet, exercise, sleep and stress — the reason for a follow-up measurement.

blocks.title: What follows from this
items: Two red epigenetic values — LINE-1 (2/9) and miR-21 (3/9); the genetic MTHFR variant (2/9) depends on the same metabolic pathway. This is the central starting point of this report.
Two green values — inflammation regulation (7/9) and miR-155 (8/9) are in the optimal range and should be kept there.
A follow-up measurement is meaningful after 4 to 6 months at the earliest.

blocks.caption: Epigenetic status
blocks.title: Methylation.
blocks.lead: DNA methylation shows how active your genes currently are. Unlike the genes themselves, these values can be changed.

items.name: LINE-1
items.intro: LINE-1 elements make up around 17 % of the genome. Their methylation is regarded as a marker of global DNA regulation.
items.text: This marker is most effectively supported through the nutrients involved in folate metabolism — which gains additional importance given your MTHFR variant (genetic 2/9).

rows: green leafy vegetables, tomato, pulses, nuts, sprouts
Brazil nuts, sesame, soya, peas, leafy vegetables

items.name: Inflammation regulation (IL-6 & TNF-α)
items.intro: Combined score from the methylation of both gene regions — not the acute blood level. Individual values: IL-6 8/9 · TNF-α 6/9.
items.text: A plant-focused, low-inflammatory diet continues to support this area.

rows: grape skins, raspberry seeds, blueberries, peanuts
Let onions stand for 10 min after chopping

blocks.caption: Epigenetic status
blocks.title: microRNA.
blocks.lead: microRNAs fine-tune the activity of your genes and reflect current metabolic and inflammatory activity. Like methylation, they can be influenced through lifestyle.

items.name: miR-21
items.intro: Worsens with more pronounced inflammatory activity as well as with a poor zinc and folate supply.
items.text: With a red or amber value, a normal BMI should be aimed for; in addition, targeted zinc and folate intake is worthwhile. Antioxidant micronutrients such as vitamin D, vitamin E and lycopene as well as resveratrol support immune regulation.

rows: pumpkin seeds, oats, lentils, cheese, beef
A poor zinc supply worsens this value
A poor folate supply worsens this value

items.name: miR-155
items.category: FTO regulation and adipose tissue formation
items.intro: Central regulator of immune and inflammatory responses; influences the formation of brown and beige adipose tissue.
items.text: Exercise, fasting and cold stimuli have a favourable effect here and influence the FTO effect positively — particularly relevant because your genetic FTO evaluation is 2/9.

rows: Demonstrably has a favourable effect on this value
cold showers, ice bathing, cool rooms

blocks.caption: Genetics · Macronutrients
blocks.title: Metabolic type: balanced type.
blocks.lead: Your metabolism does not particularly favour any one of the three macronutrients. The general recommendation of the DACH reference values therefore applies to you. More important in your case is the quality of the foods.
rows: Wholegrains, pulses and vegetables as the basis

blocks.caption: Genetics · Exercise
blocks.title: Exercise type: endurance type.
blocks.lead: Both ACE and ACTN3 point to a predisposition for endurance performance. For context: genetics explains only up to around 20 % of the difference between strength and endurance performance — training, diet and consistency have by far the greater influence.
rows: Rather endurance — variant associated with better oxygen utilisation and efficiency.
Rather endurance — XX type without α-actinin-3, more slow, endurance-oriented muscle fibres.

items.name: Weight loss through exercise
items.intro: Genotype AT (heterozygous). How much exercise alone contributes to weight loss.
items.text: In your case, exercise alone leads to weight loss somewhat more slowly than with other genotypes. The effect on fitness and metabolic health remains unchanged — for weight reduction, the combination of exercise and dietary adjustment is particularly worthwhile.

rows: Maintains muscle mass and metabolic activity
With FTO, the most effective additional lever

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.title: Your three focus areas.
blocks.lead: From 21 genes and four epigenetic markers, three areas emerge in which effort and effect meet most clearly in your case.

focuses.title: Methylation metabolism — folate, B vitamins, zinc
focuses.text: Three values point in the same direction: LINE-1 2/9 (epigenetic), miR-21 3/9 (epigenetic) and folate/MTHFR 2/9 (genetic) — all three depend on the same metabolic pathway. This area is at the same time the only one whose effect can be demonstrated in a follow-up measurement. In concrete terms: green leafy vegetables and pulses daily, B2/B6/B12 via eggs, cheese and fermented foods, zinc via pumpkin seeds, oats and lentils. Active folate (5-MTHF) for two months after consultation with a doctor.

focuses.title: Fat quality — EPA and DHA directly
focuses.text: Blood lipids 2/9 and omega-3 supply 2/9. Your FADS1 variant makes plant-based omega-3 sources such as linseed oil and walnuts alone insufficient. Oily sea fish twice a week or algal oil daily bypasses this bottleneck directly; use omega-6-rich oils sparingly.

focuses.title: Blood sugar quality rather than calorie quantity
focuses.text: Diabetes risk 3/9 alongside a favourable obesity value (7/9). For you, the quality of the carbohydrates counts for more than the quantity: a low glycaemic index at every main meal, 20–30 g of protein per meal and a short walk after eating. Since exercise alone works more slowly in your case (FTO 2/9), this combination is the more effective route.

controlItems: A follow-up measurement of the four epigenetic markers is meaningful after 4 to 6 months at the earliest — before that, changes cannot be measured reliably.
The genetic evaluations remain unchanged and never need to be repeated.
A comparison of the measurement points over time is reported from the second measurement onwards.

blocks.title: Questions about your report?

legal.title: Sample report
legal.text: All values, genotypes and personal details in this document are fictitious and serve solely to illustrate the report format. This is not a real report.

legal.title: Interpretation
legal.text: This report is not a diagnosis and does not replace medical advice. Genetic evaluations describe predispositions, not diseases; epigenetic markers describe a momentary state. Both are to be assessed in the individual clinical context by qualified professionals.

legal.title: Legal framework
legal.text: Genetic testing is subject to the German Genetic Diagnostics Act (GenDG); information and written consent are required before sample collection. The laboratory analysis is carried out by our cooperation partner. Polaris Diagnostics Europe GmbH is responsible for distribution and support.
